cases.C23: Penstock Labs makes controlled flow its name: a memorable, sober metaphor for permissioned capabilities and information. Existing Penstock Group and Pentera warrant diligence, but “Penstock Labs” is clear and domain-ready.
cases.C25: Runnymede Labs evokes the very moment power accepted limits—perfect for bounded AI agents. Trust/council share only a place name; sector, sound, and offering never overlap.
cases.C15: Its military precision avoids aggression: 'countermand' captures the reassuring human override CISOs demand, offering uncompromised domain availability and instant authority without confusing overlap in the enterprise AI space.
cases.C29: Borrowing Palantir’s literary gravitas, this archaic role directly embodies fiduciary duty and delegated authority—reassuring risk-averse UK enterprise buyers despite its complexity, while securing totally uncontested registries across every key domain.
cases.C27: Anchorite Labs: 'Walled in by choice' is precisely bounded capability—sober, wry, one-hearing memorable. Obscure? The metaphor repays; UK company clear, .co.uk/.ai/.io free.
cases.C17: Seneschal: delegated keys, never throne—exact architecture-of-distrust metaphor. Archaic pronunciation is sen-uh-shul; domain scarcity hurts, but Companies House clear and name instantly owns governance.
cases.C16: 'Imprimatur' literally names the human approval gate central to our architecture of distrust. The translation firm is unrelated; pronunciation (im-pri-MA-tur) is learnable; ecclesiastical echo fades against enterprise use.
cases.C18: The defensive metaphor perfectly fits contained agents and gated actions; the US 'American Redoubt' movement is invisible to UK buyers. No free domains is the real blocker — solvable via aftermarket.
cases.C22: "Bailiwick" precisely means a defined jurisdictional boundary — the core metaphor for agents confined to granted capabilities. The Fortune 500 firm is facilities management, not AI; offshore finance reinforces strict jurisdictional control. Clear CH, clean
cases.C14: "Vouchsafe" means to grant conditionally — exactly the human-approval gate in your architecture. Clash is with identity verification, not agent platforms; archaic tone signals gravitas to CISOs. .com secured, CH clear, memorable after one hearing.
cases.C26: Chary captures the core ‘least‑privilege’ ethos—cautious, gate‑kept, need‑to‑know—while remaining trademark‑clear, domain‑available, and memorable to security leaders despite its rarity.
cases.C24: The 'claustrophobia' root reinforces the promise of an airtight, controlled environment. For CISOs in regulated sectors, this precision is a feature, signaling total containment of risk.
cases.C31: Despite the crowded space, 'Vallum' captures the scale of imperial infrastructure. It frames the company as the sovereign, heavy-duty boundary required for a true architecture of distrust.
cases.C30: Provost captures delegation and oversight perfectly—the architecture of distrust. Yes, universities use it, but so do militaries and councils. The Labs suffix signals tech innovation, not administration. Ownable, memorable, sober.
cases.C11: Cautia's Latin root 'cautio' means legal guarantee—precisely what risk-averse CISOs need. Pronunciation settles as CAW-shuh. Cautio the dashcam is invisible in enterprise search. Concise, ownable, and distinct from consumer safety.
